title: John Buridan, Sophismata ([Paris, c. 1489])
edition: The incunable as scanned (Internet Archive 4OEXVSUP2_P3a, Public Domain Mark); its text layer is held as served and does not read the black letter or its abbreviations

license.payload: Buridan (d. c. 1361) and the c. 1489 print are public domain; the Archive marks the item Public Domain Mark 1.0. The archive asserts no licence over the payload.
license.record: CC-BY-4.0 applies to this seat record only.

normalization: The Internet Archive's own text layer (_djvu.txt) as served, under original/<identifier>/, copied to text/<slug>.ocr.txt with line endings normalized. The scan is held by reference at its Archive URL and not copied. No text was corrected by hand; the loci keep the OCR's readings. The layer is unreadable for the most part (black letter, abbreviations); the scan is the witness and the text layer is held so the seat says what the commons carries.
why_seated: The only commons witness found to Buridan's logic. No commons scan of the Tractatus de consequentiis was found (searched 2026-11-14: the Internet Archive, e-rara, the MDZ; Gallica refused the session); its modern edition (Hubien 1976) is not in the commons. It is declared absent at EA-CORPORA-38.
ruling: Lee Sharks, 2026-11-14 01:25 EST: "lets continue to assemble and we'll deposit and seat the whole thing as a massive batch"; the standing rule for originals-library seatings, 2026-10-18: "original language where available always".

research.study: Critique of Pure Inference (working draft v1.1) and The Production of Readers (#1767), §11.6 "the witnesses between"
research.for: the reception history of inference from the Peripatos to the machine: the commentators who name Aristotle's ἑταῖροι, the Latin handbooks, the early-modern refusals of the syllogism, the nineteenth-century rebuilds, and the traditions that reasoned about inference without the Organon
